record.paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
record.original_question: In a heterogeneous computing (HC) environment, meaning a distributed high-performance environment composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links, can one develop machine-independent programming languages with user-specified directives that both compile a given application into efficient code for any machine in the HC suite and also support decomposing the application into tasks and subtasks while determining the computational requirements of those tasks and subtasks?

evidence.quote: Distributed high-performance heterogeneous computing (HC) environments are composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links.

Machine-independent languages with user-specified directives are needed to (1) allow compilation of a given application into efficient code for any machine in the HC suite, (2) aid in decomposing applications into tasks and subtasks, and (3) facilitate determination of task and subtask computational requirements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) environment, defined as a distributed high-performance system consisting of a finite suite M = {M_1, ..., M_k} of machines with differing computational architectures and capabilities (e.g., vector processors, SIMD arrays, MIMD multiprocessors, scalar workstations), interconnected by high-bandwidth communication links. An application A is to be executed on this suite and may be decomposed into a collection of tasks and subtasks, each of which has computational requirements (e.g., type of parallelism, memory, communication pattern) that may make it more or less suited to particular machines in M.

Develop a machine-independent programming language L, equipped with a finite set D of user-specified directives, such that:
(1) Given any application A written in L (with directives from D) and any machine M_i in M, there exists a compiler C_i that translates (A, D) into code for M_i that is efficient relative to a chosen performance metric on M_i;
(2) The language and directives provide formal mechanisms that aid in decomposing A into a hierarchy of tasks and subtasks; and
(3) The language and directives enable automatic or semi-automatic determination of the computational requirements of each task and subtask, in a form usable by a mapper/scheduler that assigns tasks to machines in M.

The problem is to determine whether such a language L, directive set D, and family of compilers {C_i} can be constructed so that all three properties hold simultaneously across arbitrary HC suites M and arbitrary applications A.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open research goal in heterogeneous computing rather than a sharply defined mathematical conjecture. Subsequent decades of work (e.g., HPF, OpenMP, OpenCL, SYCL, OneAPI, Kokkos, RAJA, Legion) have produced partial solutions providing portable programming models with directives, but no system fully achieves machine-independent compilation to efficient code on arbitrary heterogeneous suites together with automatic task decomposition and requirement determination. The status is best described as unknown/ongoing rather than formally solved or refuted.
